claim: A custom password policy can turn on password expiration and set how long IAM user passwords stay valid after they are set: a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 1,095 days.
question: Which password expiration periods can a custom IAM password policy set?

qualifiers.scope: per AWS account, IAM user passwords
qualifiers.condition: custom password policy with password expiration turned on

evidence.quote: **Turn on password expiration** – You can select and specify a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 1,095 days that IAM user passwords are valid after they are set.

note: d016 (repair of iam-password-policy-custom-options, split per setting)

claim: Service last accessed data counts every attempt to call an AWS API, not only successful ones, so an unexpected entry does not by itself mean the account was compromised.
question: Does IAM service last accessed data include denied requests?

values.display: the request might have been denied
values.spoken: the request may have been denied

evidence.quote: **Attempts reported** – The service last accessed data includes all attempts to access an AWS API, not just the successful attempts.
An unexpected entry in the service last accessed data does not mean that your account has been compromised, because the request might have been denied.

claim: IAM policies are global, but KMS key policies are Regional: a key policy controls access only to a KMS key in its own Region.
question: Are KMS key policies global like IAM policies?

evidence.quote: Unlike IAM policies, which are global, key policies are Regional. A key policy controls access only to a KMS key in the same Region.
